newsitem.title: UK: Eurotunnel aims for concession deal by EGM.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel aims for concession deal by EGM.

text.p: Anglo-French Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel said on Tuesday it hoped to reach at least an agreement in principle by July 10 with the French and British governments regarding the extension of its concession.

Eurotunnel also urged shareholders to approve its debt restructuring plan at an extraordinary general meeting, which was rescheduled for July 10 after Tuesday's meeting failed to attract a sufficient number of shareholders.
Eurotunnel's shares slipped 1.0 pence to 66.5 by 0830 GMT in London.

French shareholders who are fighting the terms of the restructuring of just under 9.0 billion pounds ($15 billion) of debt said on Monday they could have enough votes for a blocking minority at the July 10 meeting.
But chairman Patrick Ponsolle warned that the debt-crippled company could risk insolvency if shareholders failed to back the restructuring.
"It is now or never," he said in a statement.

"A failure to approve the plan risks the loss of everything ... There is nothing to be gained, and everything to lose, by turning down the restructuring plan which has been submitted for approval," he added.
At least 25 percent of Eurotunnel's shares needed to be present or represented for the vote on July 10.
Regarding its operations, Eurotunnel said its first-half results would be ahead of budget.
"We are thus very confident that we will achieve our objectives for the year as a whole," Ponsolle said.
He added that the level of traffic for its heavy goods vehicles shuttle service was exceeding 1,000 lorries per day.
The company's concession talks with the British and French governments started last October but were interrupted by elections in both countries. ($ = 0.599 British Pounds)
